item.title: Many gather for national day of prayer in capital city
item.description: Thousands of believers turned out before sunrise this morning, packing Sir John Guise Stadium in Port Moresby for the National Day of Prayer and Repentance. Some arrived as early as 7pm last night and prayed through until morning, with the stadium filled with worship and prayer throughout the night.
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of believers turned out before sunrise this morning, packing Sir John Guise Stadium in Port Moresby for the National Day of Prayer and Repentance.

Some arrived as early as 7pm last night and prayed through until morning, with the stadium filled with worship and prayer throughout the night.

What set this gathering apart was the rare public alignment of political power and church leadership, with Prime Minister James Marape expected to deliver the keynote address shortly.

Several members of Parliament, including the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Religion, were already in attendance.

The event carries the theme "Resetting PNG Today for a Better Tomorrow in Jesus Christ," drawing on the words of Leviticus 25:10 [NIV]: "Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan."

Major church bodies used the occasion to openly name the nation's wounds, corruption, violence, economic hardship, and the need to protect the next generation.

A nationwide chain of prayer began after the speeches, at 8am, with several church leaders who took turns in prayer.

The program was organised by the Department of Community Development, Youth and Religion, in partnership with the PNG Council of Churches.

item.title: No confirmed reports of OBT presence in Madang
item.description: Speculations of a spill- over of OBT or Operation Brukim Tulait in Madang from Lae are yet to be confirmed, according to the Provincial Police Chief, Superintendent Robert Baim. Baim said that whilst there is no confirmation yet on this operation in Madang, police have arrested a woman on Sunday night for allegedly harbouring criminals who may have travelled in from Lae.
item.content:encoded:
Speculations of a spill- over of OBT or Operation Brukim Tulait in Madang from Lae are yet to be confirmed, according to the Provincial Police Chief, Superintendent Robert Baim.

Baim said that whilst there is no confirmation yet on this operation in Madang, police have arrested a woman on Sunday night for allegedly harbouring criminals who may have travelled in from Lae.

"These boys have probably travelled in from Lae after the Met Supt there decided to crack down on their operation. Some have probably moved up to Eastern Highlands as well.

"Although they maybe mere speculations at this time, I must warn here that I will not tolerate such behaviours in Madang.

"Those that are coming into Madang Province to try and harm our good citizens, I must send out a warning to you that Madang is too small and we will still get you out with assistance from the law- abiding citizens who are already fed up with criminal activities.

"If they are armed, we will not hesitate to get them down and make sure we send them to the hospital or put them in the morgue," he said.

Superintendent Baim stated this warning is for everyone.

"If you're found harbouring members of the group, you will also go down with them, he stressed.

Baim further labelled the so- called OBT members as lunatics who are not fit to live in the community.

The PPC also announced that an operation is already underway with support from the provincial administration to quickly flush them out.

He is, however; urging members of the general public to assist police with any information that would assist them in identifying such people in the community.

item.title: K92 Mining supports Lahanis football league club with K200,000
item.description: K92 Mining Limited has once again supported local sports and youths in Eastern Highlands Province with a K200,000 The cheque was presented to the Bintangor Goroka Lahanis Rugby Football League Club recently at the mining site and was received by Eastern Highlands Provincial Governor, Simon Sia.
item.content:encoded:
K92 Mining Limited has once again supported local sports and youths in Eastern Highlands Province with a K200,000

The cheque was presented to the Bintangor Goroka Lahanis Rugby Football League Club recently at the mining site and was received by Eastern Highlands Provincial Governor, Simon Sia.

On behalf of K92 Mining CEO John Lewins, the Board of Directors, and the management, Marcus Bai, Superintendent – Youth and Sports Development, presented the cheque to Governor Sia.

The sponsorship will support the club’s players and youth development activities as the Lahanis continue to represent Eastern Highlands Province in the Papua New Guinea Rugby Football League competition.

Governor Sia acknowledged K92 Mining for its continued support of the Goroka Lahanis and the development of young people in the province.

He said, the partnerships between the private sector and local sports organizations is important as it provides opportunities for young athletes.

Speaking at the presentation, Mr Bai said K92 Mining was proud to support the Goroka Lahanis, which he described as a source of pride for the province.

“The Lahanis are the pride of Eastern Highlands Province, and K92 Mining is proud to support the club and our local youths, both male and female. We hope this support will help develop their skills and create opportunities for them to progress to higher levels of competition, including teams such as the PNG Hunters and PNG Chiefs,” Bai said.

Bai said K92 Mining recognizes the important role sport plays in providing opportunities for young people, promoting teamwork and discipline, and encouraging healthy and positive lifestyles.

The company remains committed to supporting initiatives that contribute to youth development and create opportunities for young people in the communities where it operates.

item.title: El Nino onslaught puts water, power at critical amidst funding anomalies
item.description: The National Weather Service has cautioned, water and electricity supplies in the capital city “are critical and will continue to be affected.” The National Capital District continues to be in drought for over three months, now with Gulf Province recently transitioning to drought status this month.
item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service has cautioned, water and electricity supplies in the capital city “are critical and will continue to be affected.”

The National Capital District continues to be in drought for over three months, now with Gulf Province recently transitioning to drought status this month.

In its August drought update, the Weather Service also announced Bougainville, West New Britain, New Ireland, Manus,Central, Milne Bay, Chimbu, Eastern Highlands, Hela, Southern Highlands, Morobe and Western and were on drought alert or these provinces will experience “below average rainfall, stressed vegetation and dry forecast.”

East New Britain, East Sepik, Enga, Jiwaka, Madang, Northern, West Sepik and Western Highlands are on drought watch.

Responsible state agencies including the National weather service and the National Disaster Centre had put together a K70-million submission to the National Executive Council for El Nino preparedness work, in June.

The Government has instead now asked that the District Services and Provincial Services Improvement funds of about K10-million be redirected towards El Nino preparedness work.

These directions on top of a proposed K300-million disaster relief financing from the World Bank, to go towards El Nino.

Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey, while announcing the proposed loan, did not specify on what specific El Nino preparatory work - this funding would be used for.

The proposed loan is among considerations to be captured in the Supplementary budget scheduled for 3rd September.

item.title: From opportunity to community
item.description: When Bobby Tonny left Lae in March to take up work in Australia through the Lae Labour Mobility Program, he carried with him more than the hope of earning an income. He also had a plan to use the opportunity to help his community. Months later, that plan has taken shape at Three Mile in Lae.
item.content:encoded:
When Bobby Tonny left Lae in March to take up work in Australia through the Lae Labour Mobility Program, he carried with him more than the hope of earning an income.

He also had a plan to use the opportunity to help his community. Months later, that plan has taken shape at Three Mile in Lae.

Tonny has bought six brush cutters and presented them to young people in his community to help them organise themselves and carry out community activities.

The presentation was held at the Three Mile Community Hall, where youths and community members gathered to witness the handover.

It was a small gathering, but it carried a simple message: change in a community does not always have to begin with a major project.

For Tonny, the six brush cutters are part of his personal vision to support young people and encourage them to work together.

The equipment will give the youths practical tools to carry out activities and take greater responsibility for their community.

Lae City Authority representative Margaret Gelam says young people need access to resources and equipment if they are to create change.

“The contribution that I’m going to make is for the people’s vision board, where they can help us with resources and equipment and now we’re looking at youth.”

Gelam says the aim is to support young people, help them learn and encourage them to work together.

“We want to support our youth, help teach our students and, in the end, come together and celebrate.”

The initiative also reflects the wider goal of encouraging labour mobility program participants to think about what they can achieve beyond their employment overseas.

Melissa Poang, supervisor of the Lae Labour Mobility Program, says candidates are encouraged to have clear plans for their future, including how they can support their families and communities.

“We also want to make sure our candidates have a clear vision for what they want to achieve, both while working overseas and when they return to their communities.”

For Tonny, that vision has already become action.

He has taken an opportunity to work in Australia and used part of its benefit to provide something practical for young people at home.

Gelam says the first step is recognising an opportunity and deciding to act.

“When you see something, you must take notice of it. When you see an opportunity, you must think about what you can do to make a difference.”

The gathering at Three Mile was not a major event, but it showed how a small contribution can carry meaning for a community.

Tonny's story is not only about finding work overseas. It is about bringing part of that opportunity home.

For the young people who received the brush cutters, the equipment is a starting point, a chance to work together, take responsibility, and make their own contribution to the community.

item.title: Teacher assault condemned
item.description: The physical assault of a teacher in the nation's capital last week - a video of which went viral on social media, has been met with strong condemnation. The video shows the NCD Education First Assistant Secretary punching a teacher, reportedly over what's been described as "deliberate administrative delays and targeted neglect within NCD Education."
item.content:encoded:
The physical assault of a teacher in the nation's capital last week - a video of which went viral on social media, has been met with strong condemnation.

The video shows the NCD Education First Assistant Secretary punching a teacher, reportedly over what's been described as "deliberate administrative delays and targeted neglect within NCD Education."

Teaching Service Commission Acting Chairman, Maini Mike Ugaia, says while reports indicate that the teacher threatened the FAS before the physical altercation - which is entirely wrong, the FAS should have reported the matter instead of resorting to personal behaviour.

The incident stemmed from non-adherence to official directive instructing NCD Education authorities to reinstate a group of displaced teachers to their rightful positions, including the assaulted teacher.

Mr Ugaia says while NCD authorities complied with the order for most affected teachers, they failed to take action for one specific individual - whose case was neglected for over seven months, placed on payroll suspension, and without an income since April.

The Commission has advised its NCD Advisor to secure an available vacant position immediately and place the affected teacher so he can be restored to the payroll without further delay.

It also called on provinces to establish an independent disciplinary committee to ensure teacher conduct issues are resolved through proper legal channels.

item.title: Election law, Connect PNG and Bougainville among key issues as Parliament resumes
item.description: Parliament resumes at 2pm today with a lengthy government business agenda covering election laws, infrastructure, Bougainville, public sector reform and a number of government reports. One of the key items before Parliament is the Organic Law on National and Local-Level Government Elections [Amendment] Law 2024, which is listed for its third reading and second vote.
item.content:encoded:
Parliament resumes at 2pm today with a lengthy government business agenda covering election laws, infrastructure, Bougainville, public sector reform and a number of government reports.

One of the key items before Parliament is the Organic Law on National and Local-Level Government Elections [Amendment] Law 2024, which is listed for its third reading and second vote.

Parliament will also resume debate on the Special Parliamentary Committee's final report on the 2022 General Elections, including a motion to adopt its recommendations.

The agenda also includes reports on the Connect PNG programme, including a 2026 inquiry report by the Permanent Parliamentary Committee on Public Accounts and updates on the programme’s financing, implementation and work progress.

The Public Accounts Committee report on Connect PNG is among a number of committee reports to be up for debate and consideration.

Members are also expected to continue debate on the Bi-Partisan Parliamentary Committee on Bougainville Matters report on nationwide public consultations conducted on the 2019 Bougainville referendum.

Another item on the agenda is the 2026 Inquiry into Log Export Monitoring, conducted by the Special Parliamentary Committee on Public Sector Reform and Service Delivery.

Parliament will also consider a number of annual reports and ministerial statements covering the judiciary, education, health, treasury, immigration, public service, housing, foreign affairs and law and order.

Among the proposed legislation listed for presentation is a bill from the Minister for Fisheries and Marine Resources to alter the Organic Law on Papua New Guinea’s ownership of hydrocarbons and minerals and the consolidation and commercialisation of Papua New Guinea’s business.

The Minister for Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology and Sports is also expected to present legislation for the establishment and incorporation of Pacific Adventist University and the repeal of the Pacific Adventist University Act 1997.

In private business, East New Britain Provincial Member Michael Marum will be presenting a bill to establish and regulate free zones in East New Britain as a pilot scheme, including the establishment of the East New Britain Free Zones Corporation.

Goilala MP Casmiro Aia will be presenting a bill to amend the Parliamentary Service Act 1997.

With Parliament’s agenda extending across a wide range of policy, legislative and oversight matters, attention will be on the debates and decisions arising when the House resumes at 2pm.

item.title: Lae police issue hard warning to OBT gangs
item.description: Lae Metropolitan Police Commander Chief Superintendent Chris Kunyanban has issued a strong warning to Operation Brukim Tulait, or OBT, gangs, saying police will continue targeted operations to identify and arrest those behind the crimes. Kunyanban's warning comes amid growing concern in Lae over reports of breaking, entering and stealing, as well as armed robberies carried out during the early hou
item.content:encoded:
Lae Metropolitan Police Commander Chief Superintendent Chris Kunyanban has issued a strong warning to Operation Brukim Tulait, or OBT, gangs, saying police will continue targeted operations to identify and arrest those behind the crimes.

Kunyanban's warning comes amid growing concern in Lae over reports of breaking, entering and stealing, as well as armed robberies carried out during the early hours of the morning.

He said OBT groups often operate in large numbers and, in some cases, involve women and children.

The commander said police would not allow criminals to use the cover of darkness and numbers to terrorise communities.

“My warning to the OBT gang is that you stop doing this crime or you will not live long,” Kunyanban said.

He said police intelligence gathering and targeted raids against suspected OBT members would continue.

Kunyanban also issued a direct warning to suspects who carry firearms and attempt to use them against police or members of the public.

“My personnel will not hesitate to defend themselves or people who are threatened with firearms. Take this seriously,” he said.

The commander said police were also working with communities to strengthen security through recognised neighbourhood watch groups.

He said community members could play an important role by reporting suspicious activity and sharing information with police.

However, he warned residents not to take the law into their own hands.

Kunyanban said neighbourhood watch groups must operate under clear guidelines and work closely with police.

He said some people were already using fears surrounding OBT to target others.

“The fear now is that the people or the neighbourhood watch group might abuse the concept rather than address genuine OBT threats,” he said.

Police will now work with sub-station commanders to identify and register legitimate neighbourhood watch groups across Lae.

Standard Operating Procedures will also be developed to guide the groups on how to respond to suspected criminal activity.

Kunyanban said the police response would be based on intelligence, community cooperation and targeted operations.

He also warned against attempts to use the OBT situation for political purposes.

“People's lives must not be used for political gain,” he said.

The commander said the responsibility for making Lae safe rested with both police and the wider community.

He urged residents to remain vigilant, report suspicious activity and allow police to deal with suspected criminals.

“Let's all work together to make Lae safe and peaceful for everyone living and visiting Lae,” Kunyanban said.

item.title: Gun amnesty pushes for safer communities
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s gun amnesty is about more than collecting illegal firearms, with Police Minister Sir John Pundari saying the programme is a national effort to reduce violence and make communities safer.

item.title: Pundari challenges police to remain independent ahead of 2027 election
item.description: Police Minister Sir John Pundari says officers must stay true to the oath they took to serve the people and the country and must not allow political interests to influence their work.
